title: Nineteen years, 31 moments
lede: From a site for group action to a marketplace a fraction of its former size. The last entries are from the most recent filings. Select a thread to filter.

events.title: The Point launches
events.text: A website for organizing group action that only takes effect once a “tipping point” of people agree to take part.

events.title: Incorporated as ThePoint.com, Inc.
events.text: The Delaware corporation that later becomes Groupon, Inc.

events.title: Groupon starts as a side project
events.text: The first deals are sold in Chicago from groupon.thepoint.com. Revenue for 2008 is $5,000.

events.title: The company turns fully to Groupon
events.text: “By January 2009, its popularity soaring, we had fully shifted our attention to Groupon,” Mason later wrote. Revenue for 2009 is $14.5M.

events.title: Google’s offer is turned down
events.text: Fortune reports that the board rejected offers of around $6 billion. Revenue for 2010 is $312.9M, with a net loss of $389.6M.

events.title: The Super Bowl ads
events.text: Three spots parody charity appeals for Tibet, the rainforest and whales. By February 11 the company has apologized and pulled them.

events.title: Facebook ends its deals test
events.text: “After testing Deals for four months, we’ve decided to end our Deals product,” a spokesperson says.

events.title: 142.9M subscribers, 10,418 employees
events.text: The prospectus counts 142,865,836 subscribers, 29.5M cumulative customers and operations in 45 countries.

events.title: IPO at $20
events.text: 35 million shares raise $700M. The stock closes at $26.11, valuing the company at $16.7 billion.

events.title: 11,471 employees at year-end
events.text: 8,782 of them work outside North America. Active customers are 33.7M, up from 8.9M a year earlier.

events.title: Fourth-quarter results revised
events.text: Revenue is cut by $14.3M and net income by $22.6M for higher refunds. The annual report discloses a material weakness in internal controls.

events.title: Andrew Mason is replaced
events.text: Eric Lefkofsky and Ted Leonsis take over in an interim Office of the Chief Executive. Mason’s letter to staff says he was fired.

events.title: Google shuts its self-serve offers product
events.text: A local search analyst reports that Google is closing the Offers tool in its Places dashboard.

events.title: The peak: 53.9M active customers
events.text: Groupon has 11,843 employees and sells in 47 countries. Gross billings for the year are $7.6 billion as first reported.

events.title: Control of Ticket Monster sold
events.text: Groupon sells a controlling stake in its Korean subsidiary and books a $202.2M pre-tax gain.

events.title: International restructuring
events.text: The board approves workforce cuts abroad. During 2015 the company ceases operations in 13 countries (derived: six plus seven).

events.title: Amazon Local closes
events.text: Amazon stops selling daily deals. “We’ve learned a great deal from the daily deals business,” a spokesperson says.

events.title: Groupon takes over LivingSocial
events.text: The price is “not material.” Groupon also says it will operate in 15 countries, down from 27.

events.title: A second, lower peak
events.text: Active customers reach 49.5M with LivingSocial included. Employees: 6,672 (derived sum of two segments).

events.title: Exit from Goods announced
events.text: Groupon says it will “exit the Goods category by the end of 2020.” Goods had been half of 2019 revenue.

events.title: About 2,800 jobs cut or furloughed
events.text: A multi-phase restructuring in response to the pandemic. Goods will continue only “as a third-party marketplace partner.”

events.title: 1-for-20 reverse stock split
events.text: Every 20 shares are combined into one after stockholders approve the plan on June 9.

events.title: A year of contraction
events.text: Revenue falls to $1.42B from $2.22B. Active customers fall to 29.6M from 43.6M. Employees: 4,159.

events.title: Another restructuring plan
events.text: The plan is expected to remove about 1,000 positions in two phases, and the year ends with 2,904 employees.

events.title: Going-concern language
events.text: The annual report says conditions “raise substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern.”

events.title: Pale Fire’s co-founder becomes CEO
events.text: Dusan Senkypl replaces Kedar Deshpande on an interim basis. Pale Fire Capital holds nearly 22% of the shares.

events.title: $80.0M rights offering closes
events.text: 7,079,646 shares are sold at $11.30. Management concludes that substantial doubt no longer exists.

events.title: Senkypl made permanent CEO
events.text: He had been interim chief executive since March 2023.

events.title: 2025 results: a small increase
events.text: Revenue of $498.4M, up 1%. Gross billings of $1.67B, up 7%. A net loss attributable to Groupon of $83.5M.

events.title: Up to 400 more positions to go
events.text: The board approves a restructuring plan tied to rebuilding Groupon “as an AI-native company.”

events.title: Latest filing
events.text: First-half revenue is $241.9M. Active customers are 16.1M. Cash is $226.3M and total equity is negative $72.1M.
